source: VVOB Cambodia / MAFF Kampong Thom Provincial Department of Agriculture — IPM and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Rice, 9-point training presentation, presenter Mr. Tem Seng, Oct 5, 2010 (training slide deck; no elibrary URL visible)
text: For transplanting, seedlings around 15-20 days old are recommended, set out in hills of 2-3 seedlings each (using straight-row planting for easier weeding and management). Spacing should be adjusted to soil fertility: on less fertile soil, farmers are advised to plant more closely, around 20 cm x 20 cm between hills, so total plant population is higher to compensate for lower per-hill vigor; on fertile soil, wider spacing of about 25 cm x 25 cm or 30 cm x 30 cm is recommended, since each hill will tiller and grow more vigorously and overly dense planting on rich soil can lead to lodging and disease pressure. Seedlings should be set shallowly, about 1-2 cm deep, and handled gently to avoid bending, breaking, or burying the growing point.
